name: Falls Ridge Preserve
unique: A spring that drops over a hundred feet of travertine terraces stained white by dissolved limestone, forming frozen looking cascades and small caves under the cliff, on a Nature Conservancy preserve a few miles from Blacksburg.
buzz: The terraces and the caves behind them are the draw, and the trail is short. Visitors are asked to stay off the formations, which people notice because the damage is visible.

name: Lyric Theatre
unique: A 1930 art deco movie house on College Avenue with its original tapestries and lanterns, saved by a community campaign and run as a nonprofit showing first run films, classics and live concerts a block from the Virginia Tech campus.
buzz: The interior is the reason people go even when the movie is mediocre, and tickets are half the price of the multiplex. Students treat it as the town's living room.

name: Pandapas Pond
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A small mountain pond in the Jefferson National Forest with a flat loop trail through hemlock and rhododendron, stocked trout, and a network of singletrack and old road beds that connects to the Poverty Creek trail system.
buzz: Locals use it for an easy evening walk and mountain bikers use it as a trailhead. Fall color around the water is the busy week.

name: Steppin' Out Street Festival
unique: Two days of juried craft booths, four music stages and food from downtown churches and restaurants, closing College Avenue and filling the blocks around the Lyric, running since the early 1980s as the town's biggest weekend.
buzz: The craft jury is stricter than most street fairs and the music is free. Locals complain about the crowds for two days and then go both nights.

name: Glencoe Mansion
customer: Architecture people, local history fans, art browsers
unique: An 1875 Italianate mansion built by a Confederate general who became a railroad and coal man, now three museums in one: the restored house, a gallery of regional art, and exhibits on the New River valley's industry.
buzz: The house is the attraction and the view from the tower over Radford is the surprise. Volunteers run it and the gallery shows change often.

name: Bisset Park and the New River
unique: A city park on a long flat bend of the New River with a riverside trail, a boat launch and a swimming area, where the river runs wide and slow through town before entering the gorge below.
buzz: The paved loop is where Radford runs and walks, and the boat launch is the local put in for smallmouth fishing. Floods occasionally close the lower sections.

name: Claytor Lake State Park
dates: Year round, beach Memorial Day–Labor Day
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A four thousand acre reservoir on the New River with a sand beach, a marina, lakeside cabins and a nature center, created by a hydroelectric dam built in the 1930s and now the water everybody in the New River Valley uses.
buzz: The beach and the boat rentals make it the family lake, and anglers work the brush piles for bass and walleye. Summer weekends fill the campground.

name: Pulaski Theatre
customer: Bluegrass and country fans, locals, film goers
unique: A restored 1920s movie palace with a small balcony and a stage that was dark for years before a community group brought it back, now booking bluegrass, gospel and classic country in a town of 9,000.
buzz: The restoration is a volunteer story and the sound is good. Locals say the Christmas shows sell out first.

name: New River Trail at Dora Junction
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A trailhead on the fifty seven mile New River Trail where the old railroad grade crosses the New River on a converted trestle, with a tunnel nearby and a flat gravel surface that runs north toward Pulaski and south into Wythe County.
buzz: The trestle crossing is the photograph and the tunnel is a welcome stretch of shade in July. Parking is small, so riders arrive early.

name: Booker T. Washington National Monument
unique: The tobacco farm where Booker T. Washington was born enslaved in 1856, with the reconstructed cabin and outbuildings, a farm trail and a visitor center that follows him from this dirt floor to Tuskegee.
buzz: Rangers tell the story of the plantation and the people enslaved on it without softening it, and the reconstructed farm is small enough to walk in an hour. People leave quiet.

name: Smith Mountain Lake
unique: Twenty thousand acres of water in the Blue Ridge foothills with two hundred miles of shoreline, formed by a hydroelectric dam in the 1960s, and now the summer address for half of Roanoke and Lynchburg.
buzz: The lake is the draw and the houses that rent by the week book out a year ahead. Anglers chase striped bass and the July fourth boat parade is a local institution.

name: Harvester Performance Center
unique: A mid sized listening room in a converted building in Rocky Mount that books touring Americana, blues and country acts into a town of 5,000, with a seated floor and a balcony close enough to the stage that nobody is far away.
buzz: The sound and sightlines are consistently praised and tickets are cheaper than the same acts in Roanoke or Greensboro. It has become the reason people drive to Franklin County on a Saturday.

name: National D-Day Memorial
unique: A memorial built in a town that lost more men per capita on June 6, 1944 than any other in America, with a granite arch, a landing craft in a pool and a garden that walks you from the English countryside to the Normandy beaches.
buzz: The per capita loss is why it is here and the guides make that personal. Visitors say the scale is bigger than expected and the interpretation of the invasion is unusually detailed.

name: Thomas Jefferson's Poplar Forest
dates: Daily most of the year, closed some winter weeks
customer: Architecture people, Jefferson readers, archaeology fans
unique: The octagonal retreat Jefferson designed for himself and built while his presidency ended, hidden in a grove twenty miles from Monticello, with ongoing restoration and archaeology that has recovered the homes and yards of the enslaved people who ran it.
buzz: The octagonal house and the restoration in progress are the draw, and the slavery exhibits are more thorough than at Monticello. It is quiet, which people remark on after the crowds at the other house.

name: Sharp Top at Peaks of Otter
company: National Park Service, Blue Ridge Parkway
unique: A mile and a half climb of stone steps to a summit that Thomas Jefferson thought might be the highest in Virginia, with a 360 degree view over the Blue Ridge and the valley, and a shuttle in season for people who want the view without the climb.
buzz: The steps are relentless and everyone says so. Sunrise from the top and the fall color are the reasons people repeat it, and the lodge and lake at the base make a full day.

name: Point of Honor
unique: A Federal style house on a bluff above the James, built by a doctor in 1815 with a curved portico and a spiral stair, restored with the kitchens, quarters and outbuildings that show how the household actually ran.
buzz: The guided tour covers the enslaved household as well as the family, and the bluff view over the river is a bonus. It is small enough that the tour is personal.

name: Old City Cemetery
unique: A twenty seven acre Victorian garden cemetery with a hearse house, a railroad museum, a rose collection and the graves of over two thousand enslaved people, run as a garden and an outdoor museum rather than a graveyard.
buzz: The self guided tour and the restored mourning traditions are more interesting than people expect. Gardeners come for the antique roses in May.

name: Lynchburg Hillcats
customer: Baseball people, families, cheap night out
unique: Low A baseball at a hillside ballpark above the James with a view of the river and the railroad from the concourse, cheap tickets and a mascot that has been through several rebrands but keeps the same crowd.
buzz: The view from the third base side and the prices are what people mention. Promotion nights fill it and weeknights are quiet.

name: Panther Falls
dates: May–October, road may close in winter
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A fifteen foot waterfall on the Pedlar River with a pool below it, reached by a short walk from a forest road, and a set of sliding rock chutes downstream that local kids have used for generations.
buzz: The pool is cold and popular in July, and the rocks are slick. The forest service closes the road in winter and people ignore it at their peril.

name: Amherst County Museum and Historical Society
company: Amherst County Museum and Historical Society
customer: Genealogists, local history people, rainy day families
unique: A county museum in a stone building with exhibits on the Monacan people, the Piedmont tobacco economy and the railroad, plus a research room with family files and photographs that volunteers will help you work through.
buzz: The genealogy help is the reason people come from out of state. The exhibits are modest and the volunteers are not.
